steps.description: Over-representation analysis of the discrete significant-gene list from the delivered DESeq2 table. Load de_results.csv (12,000 x 8: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, ...), define the pooled significant list at padj < 0.05 and the universe as all tested genes with non-NA padj, detect the identifier space and map to Entrez via org.Hs.eg.db (org.Hs.eg.db and GO.db are the only external data needed - both are local annotation packages, no network download), then run clusterProfiler::enrichGO on biological process with a 15-500 size window and BH adjustment, and reduce the nested significant BP terms with rrvgo semantic similarity. Per the user question the answer is GO BP only; the Hallmark-first then Reactome/WikiPathways workflow of the procedure defaults is not run (unasked scope), though the reference store does hold the WikiPathways human GMT if a follow-up is requested. Guard: if the significant list is under ~50 genes, switch the primary answer to fgsea preranked on the stat column (Wald statistic; the chosen side of the disputed ranking-metric rule, stated in output) with the ORA reported as underpowered.

plan.title: GO BP over-representation of AD DE genes
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks which GO biological processes are over-represented among the significant genes of an already-delivered DESeq2 treated-vs-control contrast (atopic dermatitis lesional skin vs control, 6 vs 6, human, 12,000 genes). The DE model is therefore not refitted; de_results.csv is the input of record. Because the raw counts are also delivered, a sample-structure QC precedes the enrichment so the enrichment inherits a stated quality context (notably sample_01, whose library size is ~4x below the median). The enrichment itself follows the grounded GO ORA procedure: define the significant list at padj < 0.05 as one pooled list with direction stated, set the universe to the tested genes (non-NA padj), map identifiers to Entrez with org.Hs.eg.db while reporting the unmapped share, run enrichGO on biological process with a 15-500 gene set size window and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, and collapse the nested significant BP terms to representative terms with rrvgo. A guard from the procedure handles the main design risk: if fewer than ~50 genes pass the cutoff, an ORA of that short list has no power, and the primary answer switches to a preranked test (fgsea on the DESeq2 Wald statistic) over all tested genes, with the ORA reported as descriptive only. A final report pins the database and annotation versions, the cutoff, the universe, the size window, and the reproducibility record.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind VST sample structure QC (PCA on top-variable genes, sample distance heatmap)
clusterProfiler enrichGO over-representation of the significant gene list with rrvgo term reduction

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
